blocks.x: How Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust rewires Logistics & Supply Chain — the self-correcting supply chain — visibility, orchestration and autonomous flows, engineered for audit.

In Logistics & Supply Chain, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Tele Medicine Platform and Driisti Smart Vision Glasses with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Double-brokering fraud and carrier-identity theft rise alongside ransomware targeting 3PLs; the estate mixes corporate IT with driver-facing OT.
Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — sequenced through the Achala Method with sector controls: GDPR obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Never trust, always verify — zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace — intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter — workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane — posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
carrier identity verification and double-brokering detection analytics (fraud losses down measurably)
segmentation between corporate IT and operational systems with recovery drills (operations continue through IT events)
hours instead of days via agentic remediation
intercepted in transit, not at claims

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: GDPR and GDPR. driver and customer data duties across telematics. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.
